title.narrative: Addressing critical health and nutrition services in Famine risk areas and cholera outbreak response in Sudan

description.narrative: The overall goal of this project is scale up capacities for identification and management of severe acute malnutrition with complications, essential health services, and contain the cholera outbreak in Sudan by stopping active transmission and preventing a large-scale outbreak in crowded settings through evidence-based interventions.WHO will utilize these funds linked to the CERF allocation strategy in alignment with the Sudan Humanitarian Needs and Response plan and Famine Prevention Plan with response strategy that will contribute to maximizing impact of interventions through multisectoral approaches. WHO will expand and strengthen the capacity of Stabilization centers (SCs) to manage severe acute malnutrition with complications (SAM/MC) cases. This will be complemented by adequate and timely delivery of supplies and equipment to stabilization centers and enhancing of preventive nutrition responses through early detection of malnutrition and enabling caregivers with proper Infant and Young Child Feeding practices. At the various health and nutrition facilities, WHO will provide emergency health kits to support, treatment of common ailments among children, women and other groups with integrated health service delivery model that included mental health and psychosocial support, injuries, gender-based violence with necessary linkages through various referral pathways. Mobile clinics will be deployed to meet the needs of internally displaced people in the Risk of Famine localities.The cholera response is organized in pillars as follows; Coordination / collaboration, Epidemiology/Surveillance, Case management and Infection Prevention and Control (IPC), Laboratory diagnosis, Risk Communication and Community Engagement (RCCE), Vaccination, Logistics and supplies and WASH/water quality testing.To potentiate synergistic actions of response, WHO will utilize established channels for effective coordination of response activities with other clusters, like WASH, Nutrition, Health Cluster partners and ministries of health including the Strategic Operations Coordination Center and Hubs and spokes at sub national levels. This strategy will make sure that partners on the ground are using the same data sets and epidemiological analysis to inform action. The impact of this project is the maintenance of the standard cure rate at the stabilization centers, control of the cholera outbreak and reduction in avoidable morbidity and mortality attributable to severe acute malnutrition with complications and cholera. This will be achieved through the following activities: expansion of the nutrition and disease surveillance network, building the capacity of health workers to identify, refer and treat complicated cases of severe acute malnutrition and cholera cases, procurement and distribution of emergency health kits, SAM kits cholera kits. Furthermore, through supporting operational costs for SCs, cholera treatment facilities and setting up of oral rehydration points, procurement and distribution of laboratory diagnostic reagents, printing and distribution of job aids, protocols etc., and conduct of supportive supervisory visits in collaboration with the ministries of health and partners in Sudan.The project will be implemented in North Darfur, South Darfur, West Darfur, Central Darfur, East Darfur, North Kordofan, South Kordofan, Aj Jazirah and Khartoum states for the famine prevention response and disease /cholera outbreak in all states in the Sudan with focus in those reporting cholera cases. The four targeted facilities are specialized health facilities, stabilization centers (SCs), in Khartoum (2 SCs), North Kordofan (1 SC) and Gazira (1SC).This response will complement CERF under funded project in Darfur states, Kordofan and Khartoum and other WHO projects in the Darfurs, SK, NK, Khartoum, and Aj Jazirah. The project will greatly contribute to the implementation of the Famine Prevention Plan and Cholera response plan.
